text: Proof. Let \((a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)\) be the type. By Lemma 6.3, \(Q''\ne1\) needs \(a_3\ge2\) or \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) with at least three generators; as \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is not cyclic, \(a_2\ge2\), so \(a_2\ge3\) or \(a_3\ge2\). Moreover \(a_1\ge d(Q)\), \(a_4\ge1\), and for \(d(Q)=2\) the group \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) is cyclic. So \(d(Q)\ge3\) and \(|Q|\ge p^{d(Q)+5}\), which gives (1) and the first part of (2); at \(p^9\) and \(d=4\) the bound is attained exactly by the two types listed. At \(p^9\) and \(d=5\) the only type with \(a_2\ge2\) is \((5,2,1,1)\), and such groups are metabelian.

In particular the computer statement “every \(3\)-group of class \(4\) and order \(3^5\), \(3^6\), \(3^7\) is metabelian” of Proposition 5.1 now has a proof, and so does the observation that all non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) and order \(3^8\) have rank \(3\).

Theorem. [[paper; Lean]; relies on [Tah81, Thm. 6.1], also formalized] Let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group with \(Q/\gamma_2(Q)\) of exponent \(3\). Then \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\). More generally, \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\) for every group \(G\) with \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) finite of exponent \(3\).
This covers non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) of every rank and order; for instance all \(904\) non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) and order \(3^8\) have \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_3^3\) [computer].

Proof. Reductions. For \(G\) as in the second statement, \(\bar G=G/\gamma_5(G)\) is nilpotent with finite abelianization, hence finite; its lower central factors are images of tensor powers of \(\bar G_{ab}\), so \(\bar G\) is a \(3\)-group, and \(D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_5(G)\) follows from \(D_5(\bar G)=1\) by functoriality. So let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group with \(\gamma_5(Q)=1\) and \(Q/\gamma_2\) of exponent \(3\); we show \(D_5(Q)=1\). Tahara's Theorem 6.1 is stated for any finite group with an \(N\)-series ending at \(H_5=1\) [Tah81, §6, p. 159], so class \(\le3\) needs no separate treatment. We write \(\gamma_3\) and \(\gamma_4\) additively where convenient.

Identities. (i) \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\), \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\), \(\gamma_4\) are elementary abelian: they are spanned by the values of bilinear maps with one argument in \(Q/\gamma_2\). (ii) \(P\colon Q/\gamma_2\to\gamma_2/\gamma_3\), \(x\mapsto x^3\gamma_3\), and \(\pi\colon\gamma_2/\gamma_3\to\gamma_3/\gamma_4\), \(a\mapsto a^3\gamma_4\), are homomorphisms. (iii) For \(x\in Q\), \(a\in\gamma_2\): \[[x^3,a]=[x,a]^3=[x,a^3],\qquad [a,x^3]=[a,x]^3.\] Indeed, for \(c=[x,a]\in\gamma_3\), \(c^x=c[c,x]\) with \([c,x]\) central, so \([x^3,a]=c^3[c,x]^3=c^3\) as \(\gamma_4\) has exponent \(3\); and \([x,a^3]=c\,c^a c^{a^2}=c^3\) as \([\gamma_3,\gamma_2]=1\). Consequently, if \(a\in\gamma_2\) and \(a^3\in\gamma_4\), then \([x^3,a]=[x,a^3]=1\).

Tahara's description. Choose bases of uniqueness: \(x_1,\dots,x_s\) of \(Q/\gamma_2\) such that \(x_1,\dots,x_m\) span a complement of \(\ker P\) and \(x_{m+1},\dots,x_s\) span \(\ker P\) (so \(x_i^3\in\gamma_3\) for \(i>m\)); \(x_{2k}=x_k^3\) for \(k\le m\), completed to a basis \(x_{21},\dots,x_{2t}\) of \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\). All orders \(d(i),e(k),f(l)\) equal \(3\), and the constants \(b_{ik}\) of \(x_i^3\equiv\prod_k x_{2k}^{b_{ik}}\pmod{\gamma_3}\) are \(b_{ik}=\delta_{ik}\) for \(i\le m\), \(b_{ik}=0\) for \(i>m\). By [Tah81, Thm. 6.1] (checked against the original, pp. 159–161), \(D_5(Q)\) is generated by the elements \[g=\sum_{i<j}u_{ij}[x_i^3,x_j]+\sum_{i,k}v_{ik}\sum_{l>k}b_{il}[x_{2l},x_{2k}]+\sum_{i\le j\le k}w_{ijk}[x_i^3,x_j,x_k]\] for integer families \((u,v,v',w,w',w'')\) satisfying Tahara's conditions (A)–(F) (Tahara writes \(g\) with minus signs; the conditions are homogeneous, so the subgroup is the same). With all orders \(3\) we use: (B) \(\sum_{h>i}u_{ih}b_{hk}-\sum_{h<i}u_{hi}b_{hk}+3v_{ik}+3v'_{ik}=0\); (C) \(3\mid u_{ij}\); (D) \(3v_{ik}-\sum_{h\le i}w_{hii}b_{hk}-\sum_{h>i}w''_{iih}b_{hk}\equiv0\) and, for \(i<j\), \(\sum_{h\le i}w_{hij}b_{hk}+\sum_{i<h\le j}w'_{ihj}b_{hk}+\sum_{h>j}w''_{ijh}b_{hk}\equiv0\pmod3\); (E) \(\sum_kv'_{ik}d_{kl}\equiv{}\)a combination of \(u\)-terms and of terms \(w_{gih}\alpha^{(gh)}_l\), \(w_{ghi}\alpha^{(gh)}_l\), \(w'_{igh}\alpha^{(gh)}_l\pmod 3\), where \(x_{2k}^3\equiv\prod_lx_{3l}^{d_{kl}}\) and \([x_g^3,x_h]\equiv\prod_lx_{3l}^{\alpha^{(gh)}_l}\pmod{\gamma_4}\); (F) \(\sum_iv_{ik}b_{ik}\equiv0\) and \(\sum_iv_{ik}b_{il}+\sum_iv_{il}b_{ik}\equiv0\pmod3\) for \(k<l\). Condition (C) is Tahara's (C) for \(p=3\) and \(d(i)=d(j)\), where \(\binom33=1\) is not divisible by \(3\); for \(p\ge5\) it is empty.

\(g=0\) for every admissible family. (1) Putting \(b_{hk}=\delta_{hk}\) (\(k\le m\)) into (D) shows that every coefficient \(w,w',w''\) whose distinguished index (the first, middle, last one respectively) is \(\le m\) is divisible by \(3\). (2) Hence the \(w\)-part vanishes: for \(i\le m\) by (1) and since \(\gamma_4\) has exponent \(3\); for \(i>m\) because \(x_i^3\in\gamma_3\) and \([x_i^3,x_j,x_k]\in\gamma_5=1\). (3) Writing \(u_{ij}=3u'_{ij}\) by (C), identity (iii) gives \(u_{ij}[x_i^3,x_j]=u'_{ij}[x_i^3,x_j^3]\), which vanishes unless \(i,j\le m\). Put \(Y_k=x_k^3\) (\(k\le m\)). (4) The \(v\)-part equals \(\sum_{k<i\le m}v_{ik}[Y_i,Y_k]\). (5) With \(U\) the skew matrix \(U_{ik}=u'_{ik}\) (\(i<k\)), (B) gives \(v'_{ik}=-v_{ik}-U_{ik}\) for \(k\le m\) and \(v'_{ik}=-v_{ik}\) for \(k>m\); (F) gives \(v_{kk}\equiv0\), \(v_{lk}\equiv-v_{kl}\) for \(k,l\le m\) and \(v_{kl}\equiv0\) for \(k\le m<l\); in (E) all \(w\)-terms vanish modulo \(3\) by (1), since for a distinguished index \(g>m\) we have \(\alpha^{(gh)}\equiv0\). So (E) says that \(a_i=\prod_kx_{2k}^{v'_{ik}}\) satisfies \(a_i^3\in\gamma_4\). With \(M=v+U\) (skew modulo \(3\) on indices \(\le m\)) we get \(a_i\gamma_3=-\rho_i\), \(\rho_i=\sum_{k\le m}M_{ik}Y_k\in\ker\pi\). (6) Altogether \[g=\sum_{k<i\le m}M_{ik}[Y_i,Y_k]=\tfrac12\sum_{i\le m}[x_i^3,r_i]\] with \(r_i\in\gamma_2\) representing \(\rho_i\) (dividing by \(2\) is legitimate in \(\gamma_4\) of exponent \(3\)), and \([x_i^3,r_i]=[x_i,r_i^3]=1\) by (iii), since \(r_i^3\in\gamma_4\) is central. So \(g=1\).

Remark. The exponent hypothesis is used in three places: in (C) (for \(d(j)\ge3d(i)\) Tahara's condition is empty and terms \(u_{ij}[x_i^{d(i)},x_j^3]\) with \(x_j^3\notin\gamma_2\) appear), in the choice of basis (Tahara's (D), (E) hold only modulo \((d(i),e(k))\), \((d(i),f(l))\)), and in (iii). The next case, \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_{3^a}\times C_3^{s-1}\), is settled by Theorem 6.8 below. Check of the theorem: \(169\) random non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) with \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_3^3\) or \(C_3^4\), of orders \(3^{10}\)–\(3^{79}\), \(29\) of them with \(\Omega_1(Z)\cap Q''\cap M_5\ne1\): identity (iii) holds and \(D_5=1\) in all of them (truncated Magnus algebra modulo \(3^{19}\) with the exactness certificate) [computer].

Theorem. [[paper; Lean]; relies on [Tah81, Thm. 6.1], also formalized; checked by an independent line-by-line review] Let \(Q\) be a finite \(3\)-group with \(Q/\gamma_2(Q)\cong C_{3^a}\times C_3^{s-1}\) for some \(a\ge1\), i.e. with at most one invariant of \(Q/\gamma_2\) larger than \(3\). Then \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\); the same holds for every group \(G\) with \(G/\gamma_2(G)\) of this form.

Proof. For \(a=1\) this is Theorem 6.6; let \(a\ge2\), \(\gamma_5(Q)=1\), and let \(x_s\) have order \(3^a\) modulo \(\gamma_2\). Since \(\Lambda^2(C_{3^a}\times C_3^{s-1})\) has exponent \(3\), the factors \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\), \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\), \(\gamma_4\) are still elementary abelian, so identities (i)–(iii) of the proof of Theorem 6.6 hold for all \(x\in Q\), and moreover \([x^{3^n},y]=[x,y]^{3^n}\) for \(n\ge2\). The class \(x_s^{3^a}\gamma_3\) does not depend on the choice of \(x_s\), so there are two cases. If \(x_s^{3^a}\notin\gamma_3\), Tahara's (B) forces \(3\mid u_{is}\), every term involving \(x_s^{3^a}\) vanishes by the identity above, and the proof of Theorem 6.6 goes through. If \(x_s^{3^a}\in\gamma_3\), the coefficients \(u_{is}\) are unrestricted. For \(a\ge3\) all new terms are \(3^a\)-th powers of elements of \(\gamma_3\) and vanish. For \(a=2\) the new term \(\sum_iu_{is}[x_i^9,x_s]\) of \(g\) cancels only half of the pairing \(\tfrac12\sum_i[x_i^3,r_i]\), which (E) now gives as \(-\sum_iu_{is}[x_i,x_s]^9\); the remainder is \(\tfrac12[r_s^3,x_s]\) with \(r_s=\prod_ix_i^{3u_{is}}\), and condition (E) for the row \(s\), which sees \(u_{is}\) through (B) with \(d(s)/d(i)=3\), gives \(r_s^3\in\gamma_4\). So \(g=1\) for every admissible family. (This step is not void: there are groups of order \(3^{16}\) with \(x_s^9\in\gamma_3\) and \([x_i^9,x_s]\ne1\) [computer].) Here \(\alpha^{(ss)}=0\) is read off Tahara's generators of types (V), (VI) [Tah81, pp. 150–151]. Details: wiki, MATH-135.

Consequently a minimal \(3\)-group with \(D_5\ne\gamma_5\) has at least two invariants \(\ge9\) in \(Q/\gamma_2\), so \(|Q/\gamma_2|\ge3^5\). Checks: random non-metabelian groups of class \(4\) with \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_9\times C_3^{s-1}\), \(s=2,3,4\), and \(C_{27},C_{81}\times C_3^{s-1}\), including the case \(x_s^{3^a}\in\gamma_3\) [computer; runs in progress].

For a \(p\)-group \(P\) of \(p\)-class \(c\) let \(P^*\) be its \(p\)-covering group, \(M\le Z(P^*)\) the multiplier (elementary abelian, \(P^*/M\cong P\)) and \(N=P_{c+1}(P^*)\le M\) the nucleus [OBr90]. The immediate descendants of step size \(1\) are the \(Q=P^*/U\), \(U<M\) of index \(p\) with \(N\not\le U\), and then \(\langle z\rangle=M/U\) is central of order \(p\) with \(Q/\langle z\rangle\cong P\).

Lemma (a filter on parents). If one of \(M\cap P^{*\prime\prime}\), \(M\cap M_5(P^*)\), \(N\) and, when \(P\) has class \(3\), \(\gamma_4(P^*)\), lies in \(\gamma_5(P^*)\), then no immediate descendant \(Q\) of step size \(1\) of \(P\) is of class \(4\) with \(z\in Q''\cap M_5(Q)\).

Proof. \(\gamma_n\), derived subgroups and the Jennings subgroups \(M_n=\prod_{ip^j\ge n}\gamma_i^{p^j}\) pass to quotients: \(X(P^*/U)=X(P^*)U/U\). Class \(4\) needs \(\gamma_5(P^*)\le U\) (and \(\gamma_4(P^*)
ot\le U\) if \(P\) has class \(3\)); \(z\in Q''\) needs \(M\cap P^{*\prime\prime}
ot\le U\); \(z\in M_5(Q)\) needs \(M\cap M_5(P^*)
ot\le U\); and \(N
ot\le U\).

Theorem ([paper]). Let \(p\) be odd and \(P\) a finite \(p\)-group of class \(3\) with \(|\gamma_2(P)/\gamma_3(P)|=p^2\) and \(|\gamma_3(P)|=p\). Then \(P^{*\prime\prime}=1\). In particular every immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of \(P\) is metabelian, and \(P\) is rejected by Lemma 6.9.

Proof. \(P''\subseteq\gamma_4(P)=1\), so \(P^{*\prime\prime}\le M\), and as the subgroups \(U\) of index \(p\) in \(M\) intersect trivially it suffices to show \(Q''=1\) for \(Q=P^*/U\). Here \(\gamma_4(Q)\le\langle z\rangle\). If \(z\notin\gamma_2(Q)\), then \(\gamma_2(Q)\cong\gamma_2(P)\) is abelian. If \(z\in\gamma_2(Q)\setminus\gamma_4(Q)\), then \(\gamma_4(Q)=1\) and \(Q''\subseteq\gamma_4(Q)=1\). If \(z\in\gamma_4(Q)\), then \(Q\) has the same factors \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\), \(\gamma_3/\gamma_4\) as \(P\), and Lemma 6.3 gives \(Q''\subseteq\gamma_5(Q)=1\). (Lemma 6.3 does not apply to \(P^*\) itself, whose lower central factors are larger.)

Remark. • For \(p=2\) the theorem fails: SmallGroup\((64,138)\) has type \((3,2,1)\), while its \(2\)-covering group has order \(2^{13}\), class \(4\) and \(|P^{*\prime\prime}|=2\); likewise SmallGroup\((128,i)\), \(i=522,599,621,1755\), and \(12\) groups of order \(2^8\) [computer]. • Check: the hypothesis holds for \(13\,315\) groups of order \(3^8\) and \(2\,754\) of order \(7^7\), and \(P^{*\prime\prime}=1\) in all of them [computer]. • The theorem does not say that such \(P\) are terminal. Of the \(7\,824\) groups of order \(3^8\) and type \((5,2,1)\) (SmallGroup\((3^8,i)\), \(1\,387\,558\le i\le1\,395\,381\)), \(190\) have nucleus of order \(3\), e.g. SmallGroup\((81,9)\times3^{1+2}_+\times C_3\), and all of their descendants are metabelian of type \((5,2,1,1)\) [computer]. For \(P/\gamma_2\) elementary abelian, nonterminality needs \(|Z(P)\cap\gamma_2(P)|=p^2\), \(\gamma_2(P)\) elementary abelian and \(P^p\le Z(P)\), and for \(p=3\) a further linear condition over \(\mathbb F_3\) [paper]; these conditions hold for the \(190\) but also for \(573\) terminal groups, and an exact criterion is open [open].

Theorem ([computer + paper]). \(D_5(Q)=\gamma_5(Q)\) for every \(3\)-group \(Q\) of order at most \(3^9\). Hence \(D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)\) has no \(3\)-torsion for every finite group \(G\) whose Sylow \(3\)-subgroup has order at most \(3^9\).

Proof. By Theorem 5.4(3) a counterexample \(Q\) of least order has order \(3^8\) or \(3^9\), and Lemma 6.2 applies to it; for order \(3^9\) we may use the result for order \(3^8\). The deduction for \(G\) is as in Theorem 5.4.

Order \(3^8\). Every group is in the SmallGroups library (package sglppow). Of the \(1\,396\,077\) groups, \(904\) are non-metabelian of class \(4\); all have rank \(3\) (as they must, Proposition 6.5), \(|Z|=|Q''|=|\gamma_4|=3\) and \(Q/\gamma_2\cong C_3^3\), types \((3,2,2,1)\) (\(889\)) and \((3,3,1,1)\) (\(15\)) [computer]. So Theorem 6.6 gives \(D_5=1\) for all of them. Independently, \(699\) of them have \(z\in Q''\cap M_5\), and for each the truncated Magnus algebra (\(121\) monomials, modulo \(3^{19}\), with the exactness certificate \(3^{18}\Delta\subseteq\Delta^5+3^{19}\)) gives \(z\notin D_5\) [computer].

Order \(3^9\). Let \(Q\) be a counterexample and \(P=Q/\langle zangle\), of order \(3^8\) and class \(3\) or \(4\). By Proposition 6.5(2), \(d(Q)\in\{3,4\}\); the case \(d(Q)=5\), type \((5,2,1,1)\), is excluded on paper (alternatively, by Theorem 6.10: all \(7\,824\) possible parents are rejected by Lemma 6.9, as a full run confirms). For \(d\in\{3,4\}\) [computer]: of the \(771\,597\) groups \(P\) of order \(3^8\), rank \(3\) or \(4\) and class \(3\) or \(4\), \(3\,986\) pass the filter of Lemma 6.9; ANUPQ lists their \(305\,583\) immediate descendants of step size \(1\); \(64\,362\) have class \(4\), \(Q''
e1\) and cyclic centre, and \(62\,245\) of these have \(z\in Q''\cap M_5\). For each of the \(62\,245\) the truncated Magnus algebra gives \(z
otin D_5\), exactly. The presentations given to it were checked independently with ANUPQ (order \(3^9\), class \(4\), \(z\) central of order \(3\) in \(Q''\cap M_5\)). The filter was validated against full expansion on a range and a random sample of \(1500\) parents, without loss of a candidate. The descendant step was repeated with an ANUPQ in which the defects found in an audit of the package are fixed (https://ispacex.github.io/gap/; two of them give wrong descendants for inputs not met here): for each of the \(3\,986\) parents the numbers of descendants, of groups of class \(4\) with \(Q''
e1\) and cyclic centre, and of candidates are the same, and the \(62\,245\) presentations are identical.

Cost and data. The order-\(3^9\) run took \(3\) h \(21\) min on \(4\) cores; the filter cut the time per parent from about \(350\) to \(27\) ms. Code: c38.g, c39.g (C39Pass is Lemma 6.9), c39all.g, d5z.py, chk38.g, r5.g in compute/magnus.

e1\) and order \(\ge2^{12}\) (Proposition 5.10). Using the truncated Magnus algebra (\(\mathbb{Z}[G]/\Delta^n\cong T_{<n}(\mathbb{Z}^k)/I_n\) for a \(k\)-generator presentation, of rank \((k^n-1)/(k-1)\) independent of \(|G|\)) we checked the class-\(3\) quotients of the three-relator Rips-type group of [BM23, §1.2] and of \(13\) variants (orders \(2^{40}\)–\(2^{107}\)): \(D_5=1\) in all of them, including three, of orders \(2^{84}\), \(2^{90}\) and \(2^{107}\), with \(D_4
e1\) [computer; two independent implementations agree, and the exactness certificate holds in all cases, so \(D_4
e1\) and \(D_5=1\) are proved, not only modulo \(2^{30}\)]. The method (code: https://gitlab.com/ispacex/cflint-core) was also checked against the lattice computation on \(30\,435\) groups of order \(\le 3^7\) without discrepancies, and is \(200\)–\(400\) times faster at order \(3^7\). • Is there \(3\)-torsion in \(D_5(G)/\gamma_5(G)\) for some \(G\), i.e. is Tahara's bound \(6\) attained? [open] (“Rips's abyss”, Mikhailov's 2013 talk.) Tahara expected the bound \(6\) to be the best one [Tah81, p. 142]. At the end of the paper he announced a separate paper [Tah81, p. 173], which would show \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)=1\) for his \(2\)-groups with \(D_4
e\gamma_4\) [Tah77] and construct counterexamples to \(D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)\). The announcement does not say that their quotient \(D_5/\gamma_5\) would have \(3\)-torsion, and \(D_5
e\gamma_5\) with \(2\)-torsion is known anyway: \(2\mid s(5)\) in the notation of [BM23, §1]. We have not found that paper. It is not in zbMATH, nor in Tahara's list of publications; his conference report of 1981 [THSH81] is on other topics; we have not seen his surveys in the Bulletin of Aichi University of Education (1981, 1982)\(^\dagger\). His survey of 2003 [Tah03] reports Gupta's claim that the exponent of \(D_n/\gamma_n\) is at most \(2\). Bartholdi and Mikhailov [BM23, §1] state the bound as \(s(5)\in\{2,6\}\), i.e. open. Known now: no \(3\)-torsion when the Sylow \(3\)-subgroup has order \(\le3^9\), and \(D_5=\gamma_5\) when \(G/\gamma_2\) is finite of exponent \(3\) (§6). A minimal \(3\)-group with \(D_5
e\gamma_5\) has order \(\ge3^{10}\), class \(4\), cyclic centre, and at least two invariants \(\ge9\) in \(Q/\gamma_2\) (Theorem 6.8). Open on paper: \(Q/\gamma_2\) with two invariants \(\ge9\), e.g. \(C_9	imes C_9	imes C_3\), where \(\gamma_2/\gamma_3\) may have exponent \(9\), and an exact criterion for the nonterminal parents of type \((5,2,1)\) (Remark 6.11(3)). • The group analogue of Theorem C of [IMP26]: is \(D_{2c-1}(G)=1\) for every metabelian group of class \(\le c\)? For \(c=3\) this is Question 1.1. [open] For \(p\) odd and \(c\le p+1\) the answer is yes by [GT85, Thm. 3.2] (reducing to finite metabelian \(p\)-groups); open are \(p=2\), \(c\ge3\), and \(p\) odd, \(c\ge p+2\). The plateau group of [IMP26, §3.3] is metabelian of class \(4\) with \(D_6
e1\) [computer], so \(2c-2\) is attained, as for Lie rings. Its distinguished element \(w\) is not in \(D_7\), and since \(D_6=\langle wangle\) [IMP26], \(D_7=1\) [computer; the dense Howell form modulo \(2^{32}\) of the ideal of relations in the truncated Magnus algebra of rank \(55\,986\), with the exactness certificate]: this group is not a counterexample, and the analogue, if true, is sharp at \(c=4\). A first search for a counterexample at \(c=4\) reduces to metabelian quotients of class \(4\) with \(\gamma_4\) finite cyclic, testing its element of order \(2\) [paper; uses \(D_5^2\subseteq G''\gamma_5\) [MP09, Thm. 2.28]]; about \(170\) such groups (quotients and perturbations of the plateau group, group versions of the Lie ring \(L_1\) of [IMP26, Ex. 3.2], random presentations on \(4\) generators) all have \(D_7\cap\gamma_4=1\) [computer]. For \(c=5\), the plateau group shifted up one class (five generators) has \(D_7
e1\) but \(D_8\cap\gamma_5=1\) [computer; certified], so for metabelian groups of class \(5\) at least \(D_7
e1\) is attained, one short of \(2c-2\); an elementary pairing lemma indicates that the construction would need the exponents of the relations of [IMP26, (3.12)] quadrupled rather than doubled at class \(5\) [paper], and our attempts in that direction collapse the group [computer].
